title: Queue collapse field log — quick runs and ideas
content:
Goal: capture a compact field log of a sudden queue collapse we saw on canary (region us-west-2). I want a runnable checklist + rough numbers to share with SRE and the runtime team.

Background / hypothesis:
- Symptoms: at ~650 qps (mixed short/long token distribution) we see p99 spike to 1.6s and then a cascading drop in observed throughput (requests accepted by frontend drop), followed by worker saturation and long tail recovery (~90s). Appears like a queue collapse (backpressure + head-of-line blocking).
- First thought: large requests (long-context, >1024 tokens) get batched greedily and hold GPU slots; small requests queue behind them and time out or get throttled; internal dispatch and the batching timer amplify collapse.
- Secondary factors: KV cache priming pressure, cold shard evictions, and a redlined batch size config on the node (max_batch_tokens).

Experiment setup (can reproduce on canary cluster):
- model: open-llama-13b-v2 (fp16) with current runtime kernels
- traffic mix generator: mixgen-v2 (small=70%, medium=20%, long=10%)
- seed script: scripts/mixgen/run_sweep.sh --qps 400,500,600,650,700 --duration 300s --clients 40
- node config snapshot used: nodepool-a: max_inflight=64, max_batch_tokens=32768, batching_timeout_ms=12, preemptive_slices=false

Quick run notes (raw observations):
- 400 qps: stable. p50=35ms, p95=120ms, p99=220ms, throughput=~400 r/s. queue depth steady < 8.
- 500 qps: stable. p99=300ms, some minor jitter on p95. queue depth peaks ~12.
- 600 qps: slight p95 jitter, occasional p99 spikes to 900ms correlated with 2x long requests within same batch. queue depth ~18.
- 650 qps (collapse saw in prod replicate): p99 rapidly went to 1.6s within 30s; observed accepted throughput dropped from 650->420 r/s over 45s; worker util jumped to 98%; long tail persisted after load reduced. queue snapshot: many inflight with large token counts; head request durations remained high.
- 700 qps: immediate failure modes; we triggered rate-limit fallback on the proxy (500 error bursts).

Small ascii table paste (for sharing):
QPS, p50, p95, p99, accepted-rps, avg-queue-depth
400, 35ms, 120ms, 220ms, 398, 6
500, 40ms, 140ms, 300ms, 497, 11
600, 42ms, 180ms, 900ms, 582, 17
650, 45ms, 250ms, 1600ms, 420, 36
700, n/a, n/a, n/a, 210 (proxy fallback), 48

What the traces show (high-level):
- Trace spans show a pattern: long request enters dispatcher -> batched with 2-3 short requests -> GPU kernel run time dominated by long token loop -> short requests wait in same batch -> tail amplifies because batching timer waits to fill batch to token cap.
- There are a few nodes where KV cache misses spike during collapse; prime misses cause extra decoding steps and increase per-token latency.

Immediate mitigations to try (fast / low-risk):
1) Reduce batching_timeout_ms from 12 -> 4ms on canary to reduce head-of-line accumulation. (expected tradeoff: lower token efficiency, maybe +5–12% cost).
2) Enable preemptive_slices=true for nodes handling mixed tenants (lets large requests be split into smaller slices so they don't monopolize GPU).
3) Add a cheap heuristic: avoid co-batching requests where token_count > 1024 with token_count < 128. i.e., enforce a token-range partition at dispatch.
4) Increase max_inflight by 1.5x temporarily so dispatcher has more slots to absorb short requests (works only if GPU kernel concurrency is the bottleneck).
5) Configure frontend to surface token_count in request header so proxy can apply quick prioritization.

Longer-term ideas (design notes):
- Fairshare lanes: explicit short/long lanes with separate batchers; admission controller balances across lanes. Should avoid H-o-L but requires more scheduler logic.
- Priority preemption: allow small requests to preempt slice scheduling for a tiny fraction of cycles (non-trivial on some kernels).
- Adaptive batching that considers recent per-shard tail stats to decide co-batching. If p99 rises above threshold, switch to aggressive short-first policy.
- KV cache warmup bloom: use small background prefill (cheap tokens) to reduce first-hit latency for large contexts when cluster sees more long requests.

Quick checklist to run next (ordered):
- [ ] reproduce locally with controlled mix and store full traces (span-level) for 3 runs at 650 qps
- [ ] deploy batching_timeout_ms=4 on canary and run same sweep (compare accepted-rps and p99)
- [ ] flip preemptive_slices=true on a single node, run targeted workload with heavy long-request tail
- [ ] add header token_count in client mixgen and update proxy rule to prioritize token_count<128 (simple rule + 1% sample)
- [ ] open JIRA ticket to prototype short/long lane in dispatcher (link to this doc + traces)

Notes / open questions:
- How much is KV cache the amplifier vs batching policy? Need a run with KV_cache_disabled to isolate.
- Do GPU kernels support cheap preemption on our runtime? check with @Eloise.
- Are there tenant patterns (single tenant with many long requests) causing this, or is it mixing by chance? Need per-tenant trace decomposition.

Attachments / commands I ran:
- run_sweep.sh output dir: /tmp/queue-collapse-darren/2024-09-18-1 (contains json telemetry, pprof snapshots)
- top-level run command: ./scripts/mixgen/run_sweep.sh --scenario mixed-long-tail --qps-list 400,500,600,650 --clients 40 --duration 300 --outdir /tmp/queue-collapse-darren/2024-09-18-1
- grep traces for example span ids: trace:abc123 -> shows batching timer 11ms then kernel 1.2s

Conclusion (short):
We reproduced a clear queue collapse around 650 qps for this mixed distribution. Fast mitigations (reduce batching timer, token-range partition, enable preemptive slicing) should reduce head-of-line locking and recover accepted throughput. Next run: apply batching_timeout=4ms on canary, collect traces, compare.

If nothing else, share this doc + /tmp telemetry with SRE and schedule a 30m sync with @Noor and @Eloise to pick the first mitigations to test.

Random thoughts (notes to self):
- consider a tiny exponential backoff jitter on dispatch scheduling to avoid synchronized batch fills across nodes
- log a sampled 'batch token histogram' every 5s for offline analysis
- check whether kernel-level per-request priorities exist (maybe in newer cuda-kernel branch)

End of field log.

-- Darren
